verses.78:1: Deus, vieram as nações à vossa herança, {polluerunt} o vosso templo santo: * puseram Jerusalém {custodiam}.
verses.78:2: Puseram {morticina} dos vossos servos como comida às aves do céu: * as carnes dos vossos santos, às feras da terra.
verses.78:3: Derramaram o sangue deles como água ao redor de Jerusalém: * e não havia {sepeliret}.
verses.78:4: Tornamo-nos uma afronta para os nossos vizinhos: * zombaria e escárnio para os que estão ao nosso redor.
verses.78:5: Até quando, Senhor, vos irareis para sempre: * se acenderá como fogo o vosso zelo?
verses.78:6: Derramai a vossa ira sobre as nações que não vos conhecem: * e sobre os reinos que não invocaram o vosso nome:
verses.78:8: Não vos lembreis das nossas iniquidades antigas, depressa {anticipent} as vossas misericórdias: * porque nos tornamos {nimis}.
verses.78:9: Auxiliai-nos, Deus, nosso Salvador: e por causa da glória do vosso nome, Senhor, livrai-nos: * e {propitius}, por causa do vosso nome:
verses.78:10: Para que não digam entre as nações: Onde está o Deus deles? * e {innotescat} entre {nationibus}, diante dos nossos olhos,
verses.78:10b: a vingança do sangue dos vossos servos, que foi derramado: * entre na vossa presença o gemido {compeditorum}.
verses.78:11: Segundo a grandeza do vosso braço, * {possideMort}.
verses.78:12: E pagai aos nossos vizinhos {septuplum}: * {improperium}, Senhor.
verses.78:13: Nós, porém, o vosso povo, e as ovelhas da vossa pastagem, * vos daremos graças para sempre.
verses.78:13b: De geração em geração * anunciaremos o vosso louvor.

decisions.why: The glossary row propitiári (open) renders the family *ser propício*, and 24:11 and 64:4 say *sereis propício ao meu pecado / às nossas impiedades*. Two blind readers (Ps 24, Ps 64) heard God favouring the sin, and both listed *propício* as unknown: in Portuguese *propício a X* is 'favourable to X', and with a sin as X it says the opposite of the prayer. In Latin the dative of the sin after *propítius* is the prayer idiom for 'be gracious about, i.e. pardon' (ἱλάσθητι ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις; DRB 'forgive', MS1932 'perdoa'). This verse is also said alone — the Lenten Tract *Dómine, non secúndum* (78:8–9), the Thursday Matins antiphon of this psalm *Ádjuva nos, Deus, salutáris noster: et propítius esto peccátis nostris*, and the Christmas-season versicle (Nat2-0) — so a wrong first hearing here would be repeated more than anywhere else in the family. Ruling: *sede clemente com os nossos pecados*. *Clemência* is mercy shown to a fault: one can be clement only with what is a wrong, so the phrase cannot be heard as approving the sins, and it asks exactly what the Latin asks (mildness in judging them). It is the plainest word of mercy a Brazilian Catholic knows (*ó clemente, ó piedosa* in the Salve Rainha). *Clemens / cleméntia* never occur in the Latin psalter (grep), so it collides with nothing; *perdoar* is kept for *dimíttere* (24:18; the Our Father's *perdoai-nos*), *misericordioso* for *miséricors* (77:38 has both words side by side). Cost: the Latin's word is not kept in Portuguese where its object is a sin; where the object is a person or the land (98:8 *propítius fuísti eis*, 32:65 of the canticle *propítius erit terræ*) *propício* can stay. Proposed to the row for the whole family (24:11, 64:4, 77:38, 102:3).

decisions.why: The Latin follows the Greek ὀπωροφυλάκιον, the watchman's shelter in an orchard (the Hebrew's 'heaps of ruins' is not followed). The image is a city left as flimsy and lonely as a fruit-guard's hut. *Posuérunt* is repeated at the head of 78:2, so both verses keep *puseram*; *como* gives the Latin's *in* its sense of 'into the state of'. MS1932 *uma como cabana de guarda frutas*; DRB 'as a place to keep fruit', which can be heard as a storehouse.

options.label: como cabana de guardar frutos
options.note: Ruling: the hut and the guarding both kept.

options.label: como abrigo de quem guarda o pomar

options.note: Plainer about the watchman; longer.

forms.custodiam: como um lugar de guardar frutos

decisions.why: *Pollúere* (ἐμίαναν). 73:7 *in terra polluérunt tabernáculum nóminis tui* is translated in parallel with *macularam*; the two psalms are a pair (the sack of the sanctuary), so one verb for both. *poluíram* is heard as environmental pollution; *profanaram* is another Latin word.

options.label: macularam
options.note: Ruling: as 73:7.

options.label: contaminaram
options.note: MS1932; *contamináre* has its own row (Ps 54, D44: contaminar).

options.label: profanaram
options.note: Plain in church speech; the Latin's word is not *profanáre*.

decisions.why: *Morticína* is properly carrion — the carcasses of beasts that died of themselves (L&S; θνησιμαῖα, Lev 11). Said of the servants' bodies it carries contempt: they were left like dead animals. *os cadáveres* (MS1932; DRB 'dead bodies') is the plain word and loses that edge; *as carcaças* keeps it but is heard as the frame of a car or a slaughtered animal.

options.label: os cadáveres
options.note: Ruling: plain; the next colon's 'carnes' carries the image of meat.

options.label: as carcaças
options.note: Keeps the carrion; heard as a car's body or a butchered beast.

decisions.why: The Latin has no object. The project's build for *non est qui* + verb without object is to supply none (21:12 *não há quem auxilie*, 49:22, 70:11 *não há quem liberte*). *Sepultar* without object is less usual than *auxiliar*, and MS1932 supplies it (*quem lhes desse sepultura*).

options.label: quem sepultasse
options.note: Ruling: no object, as the Latin and as 21:12, 70:11.

options.label: quem os sepultasse
options.note: Object supplied (MS1932, DRB 'to bury them').

decisions.why: *Comédere* (κατέφαγον, 'ate up'). 68:10 *zelus domus tuæ comédit me* → *me devorou* (glossary formula row); the same verb with a person as object. *comeram Jacó* is the letter and sounds like a cannibal feast.

options.label: devoraram
options.note: Ruling: as 68:10; MS1932, DRB 'devoured'.

options.label: comeram
options.note: The letter.

decisions.why: *Desoláre* (ἠρήμωσαν, 'made a desert'). The cognate *desolar* is heard in Brazil first as 'sadden' (*desolado*). *Locus* is 'place' (τόπον); MS1932 *morada* interprets.

options.label: deixaram deserto o seu lugar
options.note: Ruling: the desert of the Latin and the Greek.

options.label: desolaram o seu lugar
options.note: The cognate (MS1932 'desolaram a sua morada'); heard as saddened.

options.label: devastaram o seu lugar
options.note: Plain; a looser word for the desert.

decisions.why: *Anticipáre nos* (L&S cites this verse: 'to take before one'); προκαταλαβέτωσαν, 'overtake first'. The mercies are to come before us — reach us before we perish. 76:5 *Anticipavérunt vigílias* → *anteciparam* keeps the cognate. *nos antecipem* is understood as 'get ahead of us'; *venham ao nosso encontro* is the sense but a paraphrase. The plural *misericórdiæ* is kept.

options.label: nos antecipem
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's verb, as 76:5.

options.label: nos alcancem
options.note: The Greek's 'overtake'; loses the 'before'.

options.label: venham ao nosso encontro
options.note: The sense, as a paraphrase.

decisions.why: The nimis row has no single rendering: *sem medida* (37:9, 45:2, 118:138), *muito* (47:2, 118:96, as σφόδρα). *facti sumus* repeats 78:4's *Facti sumus* and keeps its verb (*nos tornamos*).

options.label: pobres sem medida
options.note: Ruling: as 37:9 humiliátus sum nimis → humilhado sem medida.

options.label: muito pobres
options.note: The plain adverb (σφόδρα, D22).

decisions.latin: et innotéscat in natiónibus coram óculis nostris, últio sánguinis…
decisions.why: The subject of *innotéscat* is *últio* at the head of the next prayed verse (the Greek runs on: γνωσθήτω … ἡ ἐκδίκησις). DO's verse division cuts the sentence; 78:10 must end open and 78:10b begin with its subject. The feminine *conhecida* already points forward to *a vingança*, so the ear holds the thread across the break.

options.label: seja conhecida
options.note: Ruling: the passive of the Latin inchoative; feminine agreement ties it to 10b.

options.label: se torne conhecida
options.note: Keeps the inchoative *-scat*; one syllable more.

options.label: se dê a conhecer
options.note: Idiomatic; loses the agreement with 'vingança'.

decisions.why: The Latin varies *gentes / natiónes* in one verse; the Greek has one word twice (ἔθνη … ἔθνεσιν), so by D15's test the variation is the Latin translator's elegance. *gentes → nações* (glossary); *natiónes* takes the same word. *gentios* for one of them was weighed: it is the glossary's alternative for the Nunc dimittis only, and here it would make one group sound like two.

options.label: as nações
options.note: Ruling: one Greek word, one Portuguese word.

options.label: os povos
options.note: Keeps two words; *povos* is pópuli's.

decisions.why: *Compedítus*, one in fetters (*compes*, a shackle). The Greek πεπεδημένων is the word the vincti row renders *prisioneiros* (68:34, 67:7), and D15 would allow the merge; but the Latin word is another, and it names the iron (rule 5: concrete images stay).

options.label: dos acorrentados
options.note: Ruling: the chain kept.

options.label: dos prisioneiros
options.note: The vincti row (same Greek); DRB 'prisoners', MS1932 'cativos'.

decisions.why: *Pósside* at the *vós* imperative is *possuí*, which is also 'I possessed' — rule 3's ban, and the object is a noun, so D13 does not help. *tomai posse de* keeps possession and is safe (*tomai* / *tomei*); DRB 'take possession of'. MS1932 *conserva* follows the Greek περιποίησαι. *Mortificatórum*: the mortificáre row avoids the ascetic cognate (43:22 *somos entregues à morte*); *dos que foram mortos* is two syllables shorter than *entregues à morte* and says the same.

decisions.latin: impropérium ipsórum, quod exprobravérunt tibi, Dómine
decisions.why: *Impropérium* shares *afronta* with *oppróbrium* (D15, the oppróbrium row, 68:20), and *exprobráre → afrontar*, so the figure *the reproach with which they reproached you* is kept as 68:10 keeps it (*as afrontas dos que vos afrontam*). *ipsórum* ('their own') is carried by the named subject *eles* in the relative, so that *deles* does not follow *deles* of the first colon.

options.label: a afronta com que eles vos afrontaram

forms.improperium: a afronta com que eles vos afrontaram

options.note: Ruling.

options.label: a afronta deles, com que vos afrontaram

forms.improperium: a afronta deles, com que vos afrontaram

options.note: *ipsórum* as a possessive.

choices.78:1: Bare vocative *Deus* (D44). *gentes → nações* (glossary). *templum sanctum tuum → o vosso templo santo* (as the 5:8b formula row). *vieram … à vossa herança*: *veníre in*, not *intráre*; MS1932 the same. The verse is also the Common of Martyrs' reading (Commune/C3).
choices.78:2: *escas volatílibus cæli* → *como comida às aves do céu*; the esca row names *comida* for food given (68:22). The second colon keeps the Latin's ellipsis of *posuérunt*, with *às* matching *às aves*. *carnes* plural kept for men's flesh (the carnes row). *sanctórum* (ὁσίων) → *santos* (glossary). *béstiis → feras* (glossary). The Innocents' responsory (12-28) reads this verse with *mortália*.
choices.78:3: *eórum → deles* (not *o seu sangue*, which could be heard as their own or God's). *in circúitu → ao redor de* (glossary). *effudérunt → derramaram*, echoed by *que foi derramado* in 78:10b (*effúsus est*), as the Latin echoes it. The Innocents' responsory (12-28) sets this verse.
choices.78:4: Near-twin of 43:14 (*oppróbrium vicínis nostris … his, qui sunt in circúitu nostro*): the shared words are copied (*uma afronta para os nossos vizinhos*, *zombaria … para os que estão ao nosso redor*); the Latin varies *derísum / illúsio* and so does the Portuguese (*riso / escárnio*; D39 names 78:4). *Facti sumus → Tornamo-nos*, as 30:12 *tornei-me uma afronta*.
choices.78:5: The settled formula *Até quando, Senhor, … para sempre?* (D27; 12:1). *irascéris* future → *vos irareis*. The second colon continues the question without repeating *até quando*, as the Latin (and as 73:10).
choices.78:6: *novérunt* (perfect of knowing, present sense) → *conhecem* (D44). *effúnde → derramai*; *invocáre → invocar*.
choices.78:8: The Lenten Tract (Quadp3-3 and ferias) sets 78:8–9 with *Dómine* before it; the verse reads alone. *iniquitátum nostrárum antiquárum → das nossas iniquidades antigas* (adjective after, as the Latin). *Ne memíneris → Não vos lembreis* (the reminísci row, 24:7).
choices.78:9: *Ádjuva nos → Auxiliai-nos* (the adjuváre row; 43:26). *salutáris noster → nosso Salvador* (64:6, the salutáris row). *propter … propter* both → *por causa de*, keeping the Latin's repetition (*propter nomen tuum → por causa do vosso nome*, 43:26). *líbera → livrai* (liberáre). The first colon is long (it is long in the Latin: two clauses before the asterisk). The Thursday Matins antiphon *Ádjuva nos, * Deus, salutáris noster: et propítius esto peccátis nostris* reads: *Auxiliai-nos, Deus, nosso Salvador: e sede clemente com os nossos pecados*.
choices.78:10: *Ne forte dicant → Para que não digam* (*forte* absorbed, as MS1932). *Ubi est Deus eórum? → Onde está o Deus deles?* (41:4 *Onde está o teu Deus?*). *coram óculis nostris → diante dos nossos olhos*. The verse ends on a comma: its subject opens 78:10b.
choices.78:10b: *últio → vingança* (the vindíctæ row; ἐκδίκησις is the Greek of both). *intróeat in conspéctu tuo → entre na vossa presença*, as 118:170 *Intret postulátio mea in conspéctu tuo → Entre o meu pedido na vossa presença* (a verb of motion: *à vossa vista* does not take one). *gémitus → gemido*.
choices.78:13: *Nos autem → Nós, porém,* (the ego autem row). *oves páscuæ tuæ → as ovelhas da vossa pastagem* (the páscua row; 73:1 the same). *confitébimur tibi → vos daremos graças* (D5; 74:2). *in sǽculum → para sempre* (D23).
choices.78:13b: The formula *De geração em geração* (118:90). *annuntiáre → anunciar* (D41); *laudem tuam → o vosso louvor* (50:17).

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps078.md (Latin, LXX, WLC, DRB, MS1932; no Diurnal text for this psalm). DO's Portuguese not used (D12). Glossary rows looked up with ps078/gl.py; wordings of translated psalms with ps078/conc.py (both copied from ps070). Liturgical uses found by grep in content/do: the Lenten Tract (78:8–9), the Thursday Matins antiphon (78:9), the Christmas-season versicle Nat2-0 (78:9b), the Innocents' responsory (78:2–3, 12-28), the Common of Martyrs (78:1, C3). Hard readings: 78:9 *propítius esto peccátis nostris* (the glossary's open question), 78:1 *in pomórum custódiam*, 78:10–10b (the sentence crosses the verse break), 78:11 *pósside* (rule 3), 78:8 *antícipent*.

Hard checks pass. 78:1b 'uma' dropped (+4 → +3), accepted: 'cabana de guardar frutos' is the whole image. Length flags accepted: 78:4a +4 (43:14's shared words, copied), 78:6a +3 (articles and possessives Portuguese needs), 78:9b +3 ('sede clemente com' for 'propítius esto' — the ruling), 78:12b −4 (the named subject carries ipsórum; the Latin's quod-clause is heavy), 78:13a +3 (articles before possessives, rule 5), 78:13b −6 (the settled formula 'De geração em geração'). No rhyme flags.
